plan.goal: Design a protein sequence that exhibits ATP binding, NADPHX epimerase activity, metal ion binding, and ADP-dependent NAD(P)H-hydrate dehydratase activity. Mg(2+) is necessary. Return an output protein sequence.
assumptions: The NADPHX repair enzyme family (e.g., human NAXE/APOA1BP and bacterial YjeF-N homologs) is the primary natural scaffold combining all four requested activities in a single polypeptide.
Mg2+ dependence is structurally encoded in the active-site coordination sphere; reviewed UniProt sequences from this family carry the requisite coordinating residues.
literature_search will resolve at least one GO term covering NAD(P)HX epimerase (GO:0034022) or ADP-dependent NAD(P)H-hydrate dehydratase (GO:0034023) activity, which seeds go_sequences.
A SwissProt-reviewed sequence from the retrieved family FASTA constitutes the output protein sequence; no de novo backbone generation is required.
No target PDB, hotspot list, or binder context was supplied, so family retrieval is the correct executable fallback workflow.
sequence_analysis on the family FASTA will confirm expected Rossmann-fold motifs, P-loop signature, and metal-coordinating residues, validating the returned candidate.
Provider selected a workflow template that does not match the available request inputs; canonicalized to the validated local template.
